mainTopic: Business and work on חול המועד, the meaning of חילקא, selling spices versus fruit, and the start of the פרק about who may shave and launder on חול המועד.
overview: The גמרא first brings a ברייתא that seems to support the 'trust' answer about bringing items home from a craftsman on חול המועד. That answer cannot explain taking items to the craftsman, so the גמרא returns to its first answer: one source is about ערב פסח and the other about חול המועד. A new משנה then allows covering drying figs with straw, and allows selling and certain work done quietly for the needs of the מועד. רבי יוסי says some workers were strict on themselves. The גמרא explains מחפין and מעבין. It then shows from a ברייתא that the strict workers did not work at all. אביי and רב דימי argue over what חילקא is. רב דימי's view survives one challenge, but a second challenge from the laws of vows is left as קשיא. רב הונא lets spice merchants sell openly, and the גמרא explains that the limits apply to fruit, not spices. The פרק מי שהפך ends, and the next פרק opens with lists of people who may shave and launder on חול המועד, a list that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the 'trust' answer about craftsmen
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that you may bring home items needed for the מועד from a craftsman, but not other items. If the craftsman is not trusted, it allows step-by-step ways to protect the item, ending with bringing it home quietly.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: You may bring items from a craftsman's house, like a jug from the jug-maker or a cup from the glass-maker. But you may not bring wool from the dyer or other items from a craftsman. If the craftsman has nothing to eat, pay him and leave the item with him. If you don't trust him, leave it in a nearby house. If you fear it will be stolen, move it to another courtyard. If you don't trust that owner either, bring it quietly into your own house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up its second answer: whether you may bring items home on חול המועד depends on whether you trust the craftsman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, items not needed for the מועד must stay with the craftsman. But the ברייתא lists a ladder of fallback steps for when the owner fears for his item, ending with bringing it home quietly. This shows that bringing items home can be allowed when the craftsman is not trusted, which is exactly the second answer's point.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא says both 'you may bring items from a craftsman' and 'you may not bring items from a craftsman.' The first means items needed for the מועד, like a jug or a cup. The second means items not needed for the מועד.

phrases.english: And so it is taught: One may bring items from the craftsman's house,
for example, a jug from the jug-maker's house,
and a cup from the glass-maker's house.
But not wool from the dyer's house,
and not items from the craftsman's house.
phrases.notes: These are items not needed on the מועד, unlike the jug and cup above.

phrases.english: And if he (the craftsman) has nothing to eat —
he pays him his wages and leaves the item with him.
And if he does not trust him —
he leaves it in a house near him.
And if he worries that they may be stolen —
he moves them to another courtyard,
and if he does not trust him (the owner of that courtyard) —
he brings them quietly into his own house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the גמרא's earlier second answer: the sources differ based on whether the craftsman is trusted.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that bringing items home on חול המועד depends on whether the craftsman is trusted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that allows bringing items home quietly when the craftsman is not trusted.

steps.title: The 'trust' answer cannot explain taking items to the craftsman
steps.stepSummary: The trust answer explains bringing items home, but the משנה in פסחים also allows taking items to the craftsman. That contradicts our משנה, which forbids it even more strongly.
steps.simpleTranslation: You have explained 'bringing.' But 'taking' is still a problem, because the משנה teaches that you may not bring, and all the more so you may not take.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own second answer. It solves only half of the contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Trust can explain why you might bring an item home, to rescue it from an untrusted craftsman. It cannot explain why you would take an item to the craftsman, which is a new act of work. Our משנה forbids bringing, and taking is obviously worse, yet the משנה in פסחים allows both.

keyTerms.meaning: One may take (items to the craftsman)

phrases.english: You have explained 'one may bring,'
but 'one may take' is difficult,
phrases.notes: The משנה in פסחים says you can both take items to the craftsman and bring them back.

phrases.english: since it teaches: one may not bring,
and all the more so that one may not take!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer that step 1 supported.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the sources differ based on trusting the craftsman.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Trust can justify bringing an item home but never taking one to the craftsman, which our משנה forbids even more strongly.

steps.title: Back to the first answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the trust answer and returns to its first answer: one source is about ערב פסח and the other about חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear as we answered at first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that its original answer is the correct one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer explains everything. On ערב פסח, both taking and bringing are allowed. On חול המועד, they are not, so there is no contradiction left.
steps.whatToRemember: The final answer is that the משנה in פסחים, which allows taking and bringing items, speaks about ערב פסח. Our משנה, which forbids it, speaks about חול המועד.

phrases.english: Rather: it is clear as we answered at first.
phrases.notes: The first answer was that one source is about ערב פסח and the other about חול המועד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge by dropping the second answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The contradiction is solved by telling apart ערב פסח and חול המועד.

steps.title: New משנה: covering drying figs with straw
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows covering drying figs with straw on חול המועד. רבי יהודה allows even more, which he calls מעבין.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may cover drying figs with straw. רבי יהודה says: one may even do מעבין (make it thicker).
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It allows protecting figs drying in the field so they are not ruined.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Covering prevents a loss, so it is allowed on the מועד. רבי יהודה allows a further step, מעבין, but the משנה does not say exactly what it is. The גמרא will explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: One may thicken or make dense

phrases.english: MISHNA: One may cover the drying figs with straw.
Rabbi Yehuda says: one may even thicken.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drying figs may be covered with straw on חול המועד. רבי יהודה allows מעבין too.

steps.title: Selling and working quietly for the needs of the מועד
steps.stepSummary: Sellers of produce, clothing and utensils may sell quietly for the needs of the מועד. So may fishermen and grinders work quietly. רבי יוסי says these workers were strict on themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sellers of produce, clothing and utensils may sell quietly for the needs of the מועד. Fishermen, groats-makers and bean-pounders may work quietly for the needs of the מועד. רבי יוסי says: they were strict on themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues. It allows certain business and work on חול המועד as long as it is done quietly and for the מועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two conditions: it must be for the needs of the מועד, and it must be done privately, so it does not look like a normal workday. רבי יוסי adds that these workers took on a stricter practice. The גמרא asks in step 8 exactly how strict they were, and step 9 answers.

keyTerms.meaning: For the needs of the festival

phrases.english: Sellers of produce, clothing, and utensils —
may sell quietly for the needs of the festival.
Fishermen, groats-makers, and bean-pounders —
may work quietly for the needs of the festival.
Rabbi Yosei says:
They were strict on themselves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with new cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Selling and certain work are allowed quietly for the needs of the מועד. רבי יוסי reports that the workers were strict on themselves.

steps.title: What do מחפין and מעבין mean?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא and רבי אסי argue, both quoting חזקיה and רבי יוחנן. One says מחפין is a light covering and מעבין a thick one. The other says מחפין is either kind of covering and מעבין means piling the figs into a heap.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא and רבי אסי disagree, both in the name of חזקיה and רבי יוחנן. One says: 'cover' means lightly, 'thicken' means densely. The other says: 'cover' means lightly or densely, and 'thicken' means making the figs into a kind of pile.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by explaining the words of the משנה about the figs. Two אמוראים give different explanations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first view, both the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה talk only about straw. They differ only on how thick the straw may be. In the second view, everyone allows any amount of straw, and רבי יהודה adds that the figs themselves may be gathered into a heap.

keyTerms.meaning: A pile or heap (like a grain heap)

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא וְרַבִּי אַסִּי,
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba and Rabbi Asi disagree about it,
and both of them in the name of Ḥizkiyya and Rabbi Yoḥanan.
One said: 'cover' means lightly,
'thicken' means densely.

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: ״מְחַפִּין״ בֵּין אַקְלוֹשֵׁי בֵּין אַסְמוֹכֵי,
phrases.english: And one said: 'cover' means either lightly or densely,
'thicken' — he makes it into a kind of pile.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא וְרַבִּי אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the terms מחפין and מעבין from the משנה in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two explanations: straw thin against thick, or any straw covering against piling the figs into a heap.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the 'pile' explanation
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states that מעבין means making the figs into a pile, according to רבי יהודה. This supports the second view.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also taught this way: 'thicken' means making it into a kind of pile. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches the second explanation of מעבין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא explains רבי יהודה's word מעבין as piling into a heap. That is exactly the second אמורא's reading, so it supports him over the 'dense straw' reading.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a supporting ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: According to the ברייתא, רבי יהודה's מעבין means piling the figs into a heap. מחפין means covering them with straw.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
'thicken' — he makes it into a kind of pile,
the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second explanation in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: The view that מעבין means piling the figs into a heap.

steps.title: What did 'they were strict on themselves' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and asks whether רבי יוסי's workers stopped working completely or only worked quietly.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says sellers of produce, clothing and utensils may sell quietly. The question was asked: when רבי יוסי says 'they were strict on themselves,' does he mean they did not work at all, or that they worked only in private?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה again and asks a question about it. It wants to know exactly how strict רבי יוסי's workers were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to read רבי יוסי. Either these workers stopped working completely on חול המועד, or 'strict' just means they kept to the quiet, private way of working. The next step will settle this.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked of them (an open question)

phrases.english: Those who sell produce, clothing and utensils
may sell in private, etc.
It was asked of them:
"They were strict on themselves":
phrases.notes: These are רבי יוסי's words at the end of the משנה.

phrases.english: does it mean they did not work at all,
or perhaps that they did work, but in private?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה from step 5 and asks about רבי יוסי's words.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did רבי יוסי's workers stop working entirely, or did they only work privately?

steps.title: A ברייתא shows they did not work at all
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי saying the merchants of טבריא, hunters of עכו and grain-crushers of ציפורי did not work 'at all.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: sellers of produce, clothing and utensils may sell quietly for the festival. רבי יוסי says the merchants of טבריא were strict not to sell at all. Hunters of animals, birds and fish may hunt quietly for the festival. רבי יוסי says the hunters of עכו were strict not to hunt at all. Grain-crushers who make חילקא, טרגיס and טיסני may crush quietly for the festival. רבי יוסי says the grain-crushers of ציפורי were strict not to crush at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that answers the question. It shows that רבי יוסי's workers stopped working completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי יוסי says three times 'כל עיקר', meaning 'not at all.' So being strict here means they did not work even in private. The question from step 8 is answered with the first option.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a proof is coming)
For the needs of the festival

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי's workers did not work at all on חול המועד, not even quietly.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Those who sell produce, clothing and utensils
may sell in private for the needs of the festival.
Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: תַּגָּרֵי טְבֶרְיָא הֵן הֶחֱמִירוּ עַל עַצְמָן
phrases.english: The merchants of Tiberias were strict on themselves
not to sell at all.
Hunters of animals, birds and fish
may hunt in private for the needs of the festival.
Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: צָדֵי עַכּוֹ הֵן הֶחֱמִירוּ עַל עַצְמָן
phrases.english: The hunters of Akko were strict on themselves
not to hunt at all.
Grain-crushers who make chilka, targis and tisni
may crush in private for the needs of the festival.
Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: דָּשׁוֹשֵׁי צִיפּוֹרִי הֵן הֶחְמִירוּ עַל עַצְמָן
phrases.english: The grain-crushers of Tzippori were strict on themselves
not to crush at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They did not work at all; the ברייתא says 'כל עיקר'.

steps.title: אביי explains the three grain words
steps.stepSummary: אביי says חילקא is a kernel split in two, טרגיס in three, and טיסני in four.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: חילקא means one kernel split into two. טרגיס means one split into three. טיסני means one split into four.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains the unusual words from the ברייתא. Each one is grain crushed into a different number of pieces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, all three words are names for processed grain. The difference between them is only how many pieces each kernel is split into.

keyTerms.meaning: A kernel split into two (according to אביי)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Chilka is one kernel split into two;
targis is one split into three;
tisni is one split into four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains words that appeared in the ברייתא of step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חילקא, טרגיס and טיסני are grain kernels split into two, three and four pieces.

steps.title: רב דימי says חילקא is a kind of wheat
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי says חילקא is כונתא, a type of grain, not crushed pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said: חילקא is כונתא (emmer wheat).
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי gives a different explanation of חילקא. He says it is the name of a type of wheat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, חילקא is grain that was split. For רב דימי, it is a kind of wheat, which does not have to be processed at all. This difference sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Emmer wheat, a type of grain
When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came,
he said: it is emmer wheat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different explanation of חילקא than אביי.

steps.title: Challenge to רב דימי from the rule of טומאה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says חילקא, טרגיס and טיסני are always able to become טמא. That fits split grain, but not plain wheat that never got wet.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: a ברייתא says חילקא, טרגיס and טיסני can become טמא everywhere. This makes sense for the one who says they are grain split into two, three and four: they were already made ready by water. But for the one who says חילקא is emmer wheat, why can it become טמא everywhere? It was never made ready!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב דימי using a ברייתא about טומאה. If חילקא is just raw wheat, why is it always able to become טמא?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food can only become טמא after it has been made wet, which is called הכשר. Grain that is split is wetted while being processed, so אביי's view fits. Plain wheat might never have been wet, so רב דימי's view seems not to fit the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a ברייתא)
They were made ready (by water) to become טמא

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Chilka, targis and tisni
can become impure everywhere.
It works out well for the one who said
one kernel into two, three and four:
that is why they can become impure everywhere,
because they were already made ready.
phrases.notes: Food can only become טמא after getting wet, and this split grain got wet while it was being processed.

phrases.english: But for the one who says it is emmer wheat,
why can it become impure everywhere?
It was never made ready!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב דימי's explanation from step 11 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's explanation that חילקא is emmer wheat (כונתא).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says חילקא is always able to become טמא, which needs prior wetting. Split grain was wetted, but plain wheat might not have been.

steps.title: The grain was husked, which needs soaking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends רב דימי: the ברייתא is talking about husked כונתא, and husking needs soaking in water. That is why it can always become טמא. The name חילקא comes from removing the husks.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, where the grains were husked. If he had not soaked them in water, they could not have been husked. And why is it called חילקא? Because he removed their husks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge to רב דימי from the last step. It says the ברייתא means grain whose husks were removed, which can only be done after soaking it in water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that plain grain that never got wet cannot become טמא. The answer is that this grain was husked, and husking only works after soaking, so it already got wet and can become טמא. The name חילקא is explained as 'removing its husks' (חִלְקַיְהוּ), not 'split pieces.'
steps.confusionAlert: Here the word שְׁרָא means 'soaked.' In step 16 the same root means 'permitted.' Same letters, different meaning.

phrases.english: For example, where they were husked,
since if he had not soaked them in water,
it would not have been husked.
And why is it called 'חילקא'?
Because he removed their husks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12 against רב דימי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא is about husked grain
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Plain כונתא never got wet, so it should not always be able to become טמא
steps.terutzMaskana: Husked כונתא was soaked first, so it can become טמא, and the name חילקא comes from removing the husks

steps.title: A vow against grain does not include חילקא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says someone who vows off grain may still eat חילקא, טרגיס and טיסני. That fits אביי's view that these are broken grain pieces, but not רב דימי's view that חילקא is a real type of grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: One who vows not to eat grain is forbidden even in dry Egyptian beans, but permitted in fresh ones. He is also permitted in rice, חילקא, טרגיס and טיסני. Granted, according to the one who says these are one kernel split into two, three or four, it is fine, since they have left the category of grain. But according to the one who says חילקא is כונתא, that is proper grain!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא, this time about vows, to challenge רב דימי again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone vows off grain, anything that is still 'grain' is forbidden to him. The ברייתא permits חילקא, which makes sense if it is broken pieces (אביי's view), because those are no longer called grain. But if חילקא is כונתא (רב דימי's view), it is real grain and should be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a ברייתא)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who vows off grain
is forbidden even in dry Egyptian beans,
and permitted in fresh ones,
and permitted in rice,
in חילקא, טרגיס and טיסני.
Granted, according to the one who said

phrases.aramaic: חֲדָא לְתַרְתֵּי חֲדָא לִתְלָת וַחֲדָא לְאַרְבְּעָה
phrases.english: one into two, one into three, and one into four,
phrases.notes: This is אביי's view from step 10: one kernel split into pieces.

phrases.english: it is fine, since they have left the category of grain.
But according to the one who said כונתא,
phrases.notes: This is רב דימי's view from step 11.

phrases.english: it is proper grain!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge against רב דימי, after step 13 answered the first one
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's definition of חילקא as כונתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A vow against grain forbids real grain. The ברייתא permits חילקא, so חילקא cannot be real grain like כונתא.

steps.title: The challenge stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits the question against רב דימי is difficult and gives no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends this discussion by saying the question on רב דימי remains a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word קשיא means the challenge is left unanswered. It is weaker than a full rejection (תיובתא), but it leaves אביי's explanation of חילקא as the stronger one.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; the question stays unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: אביי says חילקא, טרגיס and טיסני are a kernel split into 2, 3 or 4. רב דימי says חילקא is כונתא. The vow ברייתא is a problem for רב דימי that the גמרא does not answer.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of step 14 with no answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The challenge against רב דימי's view remains unresolved

steps.title: רב הונא lets spice merchants sell as usual
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא allowed spice merchants to go sell in the market in their normal way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא permitted those spice merchants to go and sell in their usual way in the market.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a ruling by רב הונא letting spice merchants do business in the market as they normally do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally business on חול המועד is limited. רב הונא allowed these merchants to sell openly in the market, even 'in their usual way.' This ruling sets up the challenge that comes next.

phrases.english: רב הונא permitted
those spice merchants
to go and sell
in their usual way in the market.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא שְׁרָא לְהוּ לְהָנְהוּ כְּרוּפְיָיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic, not connected to the חילקא discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spice merchants may sell in the market in their usual way on חול המועד

steps.title: Opening a store fully is only for the last יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא challenges רב הונא from a ברייתא. A store facing the public street may only be half open, except on the eve of the last יום טוב, for the holiday's honor. So normal selling in public is not allowed on other days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא challenged him: A store that opens onto a row of pillars may be opened and closed as usual. One that opens onto the public street may open one door and must close one. And on the eve of the last יום טוב of the festival, he may take out his fruit and decorate the city's markets with it, for the honor of the last יום טוב. This means: for the honor of the last יום טוב, yes; not for the honor of יום טוב, no!
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא brings a ברייתא about storekeepers on חול המועד to challenge רב הונא's lenient ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lets a store be fully open only where the public cannot see it. On the street it must stay half closed. Only before the last יום טוב may goods be shown openly in the market, because of the holiday's honor. So on ordinary days of חול המועד, selling openly in the market as usual should be forbidden, against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him
A covered row of pillars along the street

phrases.english: רב כהנא raised an objection to him:
A store that opens onto a row of pillars
may be opened and closed in his usual way;
one that opens onto the public street,
he opens one door and closes one,

phrases.aramaic: וְעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁל חַג
phrases.english: and on the eve of the last יום טוב of the festival
phrases.notes: The festival here is סוכות, and the last יום טוב is the one at its end.

phrases.aramaic: מוֹצִיא וּמְעַטֵּר אֶת שׁוּקֵי הָעִיר בְּפֵירוֹת
phrases.english: he takes out and decorates the city's markets with fruit
for the honor of the last יום טוב.

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי כְּבוֹד יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן אִין,
phrases.english: For the honor of the last יום טוב, yes;

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא מִפְּנֵי כְּבוֹד יוֹם טוֹב לָא!
phrases.english: not for the honor of יום טוב, no!
phrases.notes: So how could רב הונא let the merchants sell openly in the market on a regular day?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא: חֲנוּת פְּתוּחָה לִסְטָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's ruling from step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's permission for spice merchants to sell as usual in the market
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows selling openly in the market only before the last יום טוב, for its honor. This implies that on other days of חול המועד it is forbidden.

steps.title: Fruit Versus Spices
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that limits selling is about fruit. רב הונא's permission is about spices.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This ruling (the ברייתא) is about fruit, and this ruling (רב הונא) is about spices.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב כהנא's challenge by saying the two rulings deal with different products.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא forbids normal selling of fruit. People buy fruit in large amounts and could have bought it before the יום טוב, so it looks like buying for after the holiday. Spices are bought in small amounts just for the holiday, so רב הונא lets spice merchants sell normally.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This opens an answer showing two sources do not contradict.

steps.whatToRemember: Normal selling on חול המועד is limited for fruit, but it is allowed for spices, which people buy in small amounts for the holiday itself.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is about fruit,
phrases.notes: "This" is the ברייתא that only allows a half-open store (Step 17).

phrases.english: this is about spices.
phrases.notes: "This" is רב הונא's permission for spice merchants (Step 16).

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּפֵירֵי, הָא בְּתַבְלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב כהנא's קשיא from Step 17 against רב הונא's ruling in Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the two sources deal with different products.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to forbid all normal selling in public on חול המועד, which would include spices.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is only about fruit. Spices may be sold in the normal way.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק מי שהפך
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula marks the end of the second פרק, מי שהפך.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, מי שהפך.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the פרק called מי שהפך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the discussion. It is a traditional closing line that shows a פרק is finished and that we hope to learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. This is the formula said at the end of a פרק.
"One who turned over [his olives]." This is the name of the פרק that just ended.

phrases.english: We will return to you, "One who turned over"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the last answer in Step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק מי שהפך is complete.

steps.title: Who May Shave on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: The new פרק opens with a משנה listing people who may shave or cut their hair on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: These people may shave on חול המועד: one who comes back from overseas, one who comes out of captivity, one who leaves prison, a מנודה whose ban the חכמים lifted, one who asked a חכם to cancel his vow and was released, a נזיר, and a מצורע going from טומאה to טהרה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה that lists people who are allowed to cut their hair on חול המועד, even though haircuts are normally forbidden then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person must get a haircut before יום טוב, not during חול המועד. Everyone on this list could not cut his hair before the holiday. Some were away or locked up, some were forbidden by a ban or a vow, and the נזיר and מצורע have a מצוה-shave that came due during the holiday. So they are allowed to shave during חול המועד.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it means חול המועד, the middle days of the holiday.
Someone placed under a ban (נידוי), who may not cut his hair
A person with צרעת, who must shave as part of becoming טהור

steps.confusionAlert: The היתר is not a general permission to get a haircut on חול המועד. It applies only to people who had no chance to cut their hair before the holiday.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה sets the basic rule for the whole פרק. The ban on haircuts during חול המועד is lifted for someone who was truly unable to cut his hair before יום טוב.

phrases.english: And these may shave on the intermediate days of the festival:
one who comes from a country overseas
and from a house of captivity,
and one who comes out of prison,
and the ostracized person whom the Sages released,
and similarly one who asked a Sage and was released,
phrases.notes: He had made a vow not to cut his hair, and a חכם cancelled the vow during the holiday.

phrases.english: and the nazirite, and the leper going from his impurity to his purity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק after the הדרן in Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People who could not cut their hair before יום טוב (people returning from overseas, from captivity, or from prison, a released מנודה, someone released from a vow, a נזיר, and a מצורע) may shave on חול המועד.

steps.title: Who May Launder on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues with a second list: people who may wash their clothes on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: These people may launder on חול המועד: one who comes back from overseas or from captivity, and one who leaves prison.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from shaving to laundering clothes and starts a parallel list. The list continues past the end of this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Laundering on חול המועד is also normally forbidden, because it should be done before the holiday. The same reasoning applies here: people who were away or locked up could not wash their clothes before יום טוב, so they may do it now. The first names on the list match the shaving list.

phrases.english: And these may launder on the intermediate days of the festival:
one who comes from a country overseas and from a house of captivity,
and one who comes out of prison,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה, moving from the list of who may shave to a parallel list of who may launder.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People returning from overseas, from captivity, or from prison may launder their clothes on חול המועד. The list continues.
